correctness.rationale: For the forced-sum mathematical model the classification is correct. Given an occupied coordinate, moving a little load from it to any zero coordinate strictly increases the value because f'(0)=1>f'(x) for x>0. At an interior unequal optimizer the common derivative allows only the two levels a in (1,2), b>2; two high coordinates have a positive tangent second variation, so exactly one is high. Stationarity gives a-1=d/(exp(d)-1) for d=b-a. The Finding defines this as u but then writes Greek nu without a separate definition; these denote the same function, unambiguously fixed by the stationarity equation in Proof §2. Its strict convexity follows from (d-2)exp(d)+d+2 having zero value and slope at zero and positive second derivative for d>0. The budget has a strictly increasing branch from 4 for n=2, and one fold for n>=3. A fixed-budget variation in the high-versus-low directions excludes the decreasing branch since the second variation has sign T_n'/u'; differentiating the stationarity identity twice gives a nonzero third derivative at the fold, excluding it too. For n>=3 the value gap is strictly negative at the fold and strictly positive at 2n, where the cubic variation in direction (n-1,-1,...,-1) excludes equality. On the upper branch before 2n the gap derivative is f'(a)-f'(S/n)>0 since both arguments are between one and two and a<S/n. Compactness, the candidate list and the strict root then give all global optima including threshold equalities. For n=2 the sole unequal branch merges continuously into equal at S=4; for n>=3 the tie has d_c>d_f>0. This also yields the stated high-load limit. Independent decimal calculations give n=3: S_f=5.7456435767327244, S_c=5.7743134717251248, d_c=1.3974995195938845, and optimum F_3 at S=7 of 0.7718350579247905.
